## Minneapolis holiday-party bar shortlist
I started with The Knot’s Minneapolis **Bar Services & Beverages** results (44 listings) and opened these actual vendor storefronts in separate tabs for visual comparison:

- **Minnesota Bartending Services, LLC — Minneapolis, MN** (tab open): bartenders plus beer, champagne, liquor, non-alcoholic drinks, and signature cocktails.
- **With a Twist Bartending Service — serves the entire state of Minnesota** (tab open): full bar setup, alcohol ordering, ice, soft drinks, flavored water, and TIPS-certified/insured bartenders. Strong established option: 4.8/5 from 148 reviews on The Knot.
- **Maddie’s Mobile Mixes — Minneapolis/St. Paul, MN** (tab open): modern trailer with three beer taps, mini-fridge, sink, plus a portable bar; custom craft cocktails and mocktails, mixers, garnishes, ice, cups, etc.
- **Fusion Events — Maple Grove, MN** (serving Minneapolis/St. Paul/Taylors Falls; tab open): liquid catering with bartenders, setup/takedown, drinkware and beverages; beverage-menu and signature-drink consultation. 5.0/5 from 58 reviews.
- **Mix & Mingle Mobile Bar — Saint Paul, MN** (serves all Minnesota; tab open): dry-hire bartending for signature cocktails, spirits, and non-alcoholic drinks. Basic package includes setup/cleanup, up to three mixed drinks, beer/wine pouring, ice, cups, straws, garnishes, and napkins; custom/Airstream-bar upgrades available.
- **Petals and Pints — Minneapolis, MN** (serving Twin Cities; tab open): custom-cocktail mobile bar, bartenders, beer/champagne/liquor/wine and non-alcoholic options; distinctive add-on is floral arrangements, décor, and flower-wall rentals.

**Quick comparison:** For the most turnkey beverage handling, start with **With a Twist** or **Fusion Events**. For a clearly built-in NA/mocktail option and visual trailer setup, **Maddie’s** or **Mix & Mingle** stand out. **Petals and Pints** is the design-forward choice if you also want florals/backdrop styling.

## Surdyk’s Catering
**Surdyk’s did not appear among the Minneapolis bar-service listings I reviewed on The Knot**, so it is not part of the above bar shortlist. I nevertheless checked its catering site; the **holiday-catering page is left open** for you (tab open).

It does look more full-service than a bartending-only vendor: Surdyk’s says it can help plan a whole event and offers:
1. **Full-service catering** — described as a seamless, hands-off event option.
2. **Drop-off catering** — positioned for home or office entertaining.
3. **Online catering orders** — for filling in gaps rather than commissioning a fully managed event.

For food/beverage specifics the readable pages verify that Surdyk’s emphasizes quality-ingredient food and is part of the Minneapolis Surdyk’s family alongside **Surdyk’s Liquor**, Cheese Shop, and Sidebar; however, the page text did not expose specific holiday menu dishes or beverage packages. Their catering address is **2117 West River Road N., Minneapolis, MN 55411**.

## Nonalcoholic pairing idea: Instant Pot Mulligatawny Soup
I found and opened the actual **Simply Happy Foodie — “Instant Pot Mulligatawny Soup”** recipe page (tab open). It is a creamy, lightly Indian-spiced chicken soup; the recipe notes a vegetarian swap of vegetable broth for chicken broth and omission of chicken.

**Ingredients (serves 4–6):** olive oil; 2 boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 1 lb), cubed; butter; diced onion; diced celery; diced carrots; diced green bell pepper; garlic; fresh grated ginger (or powdered); Madras/sweet curry powder; garam masala; nutmeg; cinnamon; dried thyme; kosher salt; black pepper; low-sodium chicken broth; drained diced tomatoes; rinsed white rice; diced apple; whole cloves; then flour and heavy cream or coconut milk to finish.

**Basic method:**
1. Sauté chicken in oil until the outside turns white; remove it.
2. Sauté butter with onion, celery, carrots, and pepper until beginning to soften; add garlic and ginger briefly.
3. Stir in spices, then broth. Return chicken and add tomatoes, rice, apple, and cloves.
4. Pressure-cook on Manual/Pressure Cook for 7 minutes; naturally release for at least 20 minutes, then vent remaining pressure.
5. Return to sauté; whisk flour into cream or coconut milk, stir it in, and simmer until thickened. Serve hot with naan or crusty bread.

This would make a warming, substantial NA menu item alongside a cocktail/mocktail bar—particularly a good fit with Mix & Mingle’s or Maddie’s explicit mocktail service.
